name: INCA033989
summary: INCA033989 is Incyte's own monoclonal antibody against mutant calreticulin (mutCALR), the driver in about a third of essential thrombocythemia (ET), with FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation in CALR-mutated ET resistant or intolerant to prior therapy. The Phase 3 is EXCALIBUR-ET2 (NCT07623200): 426 patients with Type 1 or non-Type 1 CALR ET resistant or intolerant to at least one cytoreductive therapy, randomised against best available therapy, primary endpoint durable clinicohematologic response, primary completion 2029-06-15. The myelofibrosis work is Phase 1 only and is not modelled. Price anchor: Jakafi at $132,549 per Medicare Part D beneficiary in 2024, the anchor the book's other ET entrant (bomedemstat) uses; Besremi, labelled in ET since 2026-08-31, launched at a WAC of about $153,736 a year and is the cross-check. Uptake anchor: the book's measured value for a later entrant in a hydroxyurea-resistant MPN pool (bomedemstat's PV line, 0.152, from Tecvayli), on Enhertu's fitted launch curve as bomedemstat's ET line carries it.

therapy_mode.source: NCT07623200 (book trials table): randomised against best available therapy in ET with durable clinicohematologic response as the primary endpoint, a maintained cytoreductive effect; Incyte EHA 2026 release (investor.incyte.com/news-releases/news-release-details/incyte-announces-new-positive-data-eha-2026-showed-inca033989): 'most patients with MF and ET continuing treatment', median response duration 23 weeks and ongoing
therapy_mode.note: Cytoreduction in a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm, given for as long as it controls counts, the same mode the book's bomedemstat seed uses for ET. The Phase 1 dosing interval was not opened (Amass quota exhausted, WebFetch blocked)

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Jakafi: CMS Medicare Part D 2024, $2,082,741,189.30 over 15,713 beneficiaries = $132,549 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement on the comparator. Jakafi is the anchor the book's bomedemstat seed uses for the same disease, so the two ET entrants price alike; it is Incyte's own MPN drug, used off-label in ET and a candidate in best-available-therapy arms. Case against: Besremi (ropeginterferon alfa-2b), FDA-approved in ET on 2026-08-31 (PharmaEssentia release, businesswire.com/news/home/20260831907028/en), is now the closest marketed comparator in the same disease. It launched in PV at a WAC of $6,988 a syringe, $153,736 a year at 22 syringes (Anton Rx Report, antonhealth.com/fda-approves-new-tx-for-polycythemia-vera-besremi/), 16% above this figure. It is not used because it is a 2021 launch WAC, current WAC was not found, and no discount can be sourced for it. Jakafi's Part D spend per beneficiary is weighted to myelofibrosis dosing and covers part-years. INCA033989 appears to be an intravenous antibody today (NCT07448155 compares subcutaneous with intravenous dosing, and the July 2026 Halozyme licence is for a subcutaneous form; the Phase 3 route was not confirmed), so if infused in clinic it would be billed under Part B, where the book's convention differs

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention on a CMS Part D per-beneficiary price (backend/gross_to_net.py: halving lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net prices); the same value as the bomedemstat seed on the same Jakafi anchor
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.5 off list, so net is $66,275 per patient-year. Follows the anchor (Jakafi sits in Part D per lookup.py demand), not the asset's likely Part B billing; on a Part B anchor it would be 0.056604

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: reused from the bomedemstat seed (same disease, same setting): bomedemstat Phase 2 in ET (IMG-7289-CTP-201, 73 patients; Goethert et al., Blood 2023;142 suppl 1, doi:10.1182/blood-2023-179329): 86% on study at week 24 and 75% at week 48
discontinuation_pct.note: Reused measured value; not treated to progression, so the median-PFS formula does not apply. INCA033989's own discontinuation count is not published in the releases found (Incyte EHA 2026: no dose-limiting toxicities, 'most patients ... continuing treatment'; searched). Case for lower: an antibody with no DLTs may be stopped less than an oral LSD1 inhibitor; Besremi in EXCEED-ET had drug-related discontinuations in 9 of 91 (9.9%) over about 13 months (Reeves et al., Lancet Reg Health Am 2026;61:101529, doi:10.1016/j.lana.2026.101529), a floor since it counts drug-related stops only. Case for higher: repeated IV infusions add a burden an oral drug does not have

forecast_start_year.source: NCT07623200 primary completion 2029-06-15 (estimated; context file and book trials table), study completion 2030-11-01
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on the review timeline. The book's pipeline seeds put the first full year two calendar years after the earliest Phase 3 primary completion (bomedemstat: 2027-07 to 2029), which gives 2031. Readout mid-2029, filing around end-2029, and approval in 2030 even with a priority review under the Breakthrough designation. Case for earlier: Incyte could seek accelerated approval on Phase 1 data, which it has not announced (not found in search)

exus_multiple.source: book asset_revenue / asset_revenue_regions FY2025: Jakavi (Novartis, all outside the US) $2,110mm (Novartis 20-F 0001114448-26-000004) against Jakafi (Incyte, US only) $3,092.5mm (Incyte 10-K 0000879169-26-000010). 2,110 / 3,092.5 = 0.6823 (FY2024: 1,936 / 2,792.1 = 0.693)
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator: the same molecule in the same MPN diseases and prescribers, split across two filers. Case against: Jakavi is sold by Novartis's larger ex-US organisation, while Incyte would sell INCA033989 itself; Incyte's own ex-US launch, Opzelura, earned $130.0mm outside the US against $548.5mm in the US in FY2025 (0.237, same 10-K), though that is a young dermatology launch. The engine also scales patients, not only revenue, by this multiple

economics_share.source: Incyte's releases call INCA033989 'Incyte-discovered' (as returned by search of the ASH 2022 release, investor.incyte.com/news-releases/news-release-details/incytes-novel-mutant-calr-antibody-unveiled-ash-2022-plenary, and the Breakthrough designation release, incytecorp.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/incytes-first-class-mutcalr-targeted-monoclonal-antibody); no licensor found; Incyte is lead sponsor of all four trials (context file). Halozyme ENHANZE licence for subcutaneous INCA033989, July 2026 (Halozyme release, nasdaq.com/press-release/halozyme-announces-global-collaboration-and-license-agreement-incyte-support): upfront, milestones and royalties on net sales of products using ENHANZE, amounts not disclosed
economics_share.note: Judgement: the antibody is wholly owned, and the Halozyme royalty is not netted because its rate is not disclosed and it applies only to an ENHANZE subcutaneous product, not to the IV form. Case against: if the commercial product is the ENHANZE form, the royalty nets as (margin - royalty) / margin, with Incyte's margin 1 - 0.0724 - 0.2677 - 0.3988 - 0 = 0.2611 (lookup.py seed Jakafi), so each point of royalty would take about 0.038 off this share. Halozyme's 10-Q (0001159036-26-000104) was listed in search but not opened

prevalence.source: carried by the book: bomedemstat seed, 126,815 (Mehta et al., Leukemia & Lymphoma 2014, 47.5 per 100,000 on 266,978,268 US adults)

incidence.source: carried by the book: bomedemstat seed, 4,806 (Singhal et al., Leukemia 2026, SEER-17, 1.8 per 100,000 adults)

eligible_pct.source: Three filters for the Phase 3 entry criteria (CALR-mutated ET, resistant or intolerant to at least one cytoreductive therapy). (1) CALR mutation in 32% of 299 Mayo Clinic ET patients (Tefferi et al., Leukemia 2014;28:2300, doi:10.1038/leu.2014.148, PMID 24791854). (2) 33% of prevalent US ET patients received cytoreductive treatment in 2023 (Veeva Compass claims, ISPOR 2025 poster; the book's bomedemstat eligible_pct, reused). (3) 33 of 166 hydroxyurea-treated ET patients (19.9%) met the ELN criteria for resistance or intolerance over a median 4.5 years (Hernandez-Boluda et al., Br J Haematol 2011;152:81, doi:10.1111/j.1365-2141.2010.08430.x, PMID 21083657). 0.32 x 0.33 x 0.1988 = 0.020993
eligible_pct.note: About 2,662 US patients in the book's pool and 101 a year from incidence. The filters are assumed independent; CALR patients are younger with higher platelet counts, which pulls treatment rates in both directions. Case for higher: SURPASS-ET says 'about a third' of hydroxyurea-treated patients become resistant or intolerant (Mesa et al., Lancet Haematol 2025;12:e862, doi:10.1016/S2352-3026(25)00264-9), a statement rather than a count, and a prevalent treated population has been on therapy longer than 4.5 years; the Phase 3 also admits failure of any cytoreductive, not only hydroxyurea. Case for lower: 28% CALR in the 402-patient Mayo plus Italy cohort (Tefferi et al., Am J Hematol 2014, PMID 24753125); 15% met modified ELN criteria in 148 high-risk Korean ET patients (Park et al., Cancer Med 2023, PMID 36622093). The engine feeds the pool at incidence x eligible_pct, which understates the real inflow of patients newly failing hydroxyurea each year

untreated_carryover_pct.source: forecast.py derive_new_patients default; ET median survival 19.8 years in 292 Mayo patients (Tefferi et al., Blood 2014;124:2507, doi:10.1182/blood-2014-05-579136, PMID 25037629)
untreated_carryover_pct.note: Stated to show it was considered. Not a line of cancer therapy in the sense of the zero-carryover rule: a CALR-mutated patient who has failed a cytoreductive and is not started this year stays on anagrelide, interferon or continued hydroxyurea and stays eligible for years, given near two-decade survival. The bomedemstat seed on the same pool also carries forward (no value set). Case against: a patient well controlled on a second agent may never switch, which the penetration rate, not the carryover, should carry

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: book: bomedemstat's Polycythemia Vera line (a hydroxyurea-resistant or intolerant MPN pool) carries 0.152, pasritamig's fitted value for an entrant arriving after others in the same setting: Tecvayli held 10.9% of its observed population in its second full year, reproduced at a 15.2% peak (jnj_pasritamig.csv)
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: multiple 1.0 on the book's value for a later entrant in a second-line MPN pool. INCA033989 arrives around 2030, after Besremi (ET label 2026) and bomedemstat (book start 2029). No free source gives a second-line ET uptake series; Besremi patient counts were searched and not found. Not the bomedemstat ET value (0.058, the 5.8% a year leaving first-line hydroxyurea, Yu et al., Blood 2017): that is the flow out of first line, while this pool has already failed it. Case for higher: the first mutation-targeted drug, 87% haematologic response with 70% complete in ET (Incyte EHA 2026 release), and CALR status is known at diagnosis, so no new test is needed. Case for lower: an infused drug against oral and self-injected options, and the Tecvayli anchor is from myeloma. Rough check on the engine's identity: US treated stock peaks near 1,000 patients, about 38% of the US eligible stock, around year 8

ramp_steepness.source: book: bomedemstat ET seed, Enhertu's fitted launch (CMS Part B beneficiaries 864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105, 8,410 over 2020 to 2024), k=1.08, midpoint 2.2 years, as azn_camizestrant.csv carries it
ramp_steepness.note: Reused from the closest modelled competitor on the same pool. No ET launch curve exists on file: Besremi's ET label is a month old

ramp_midpoint_year.source: as ramp_steepness (Enhertu fit carried by the bomedemstat ET seed)
